subject: maths
question: If a certain sum of money becomes double of itself in 11 years 6 months at simple interest, then what will be the annual rate of interest?
solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money doubles itself in 11 years 6 months at simple interest.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

Since the sum doubles, SI = Principal

So, Principal = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

**Calculation:**

Time = 11 years 6 months = 11.5 years

Let the Principal be P.

SI = P

P = (P × Rate × 11.5) / 100

⇒ 1 = (Rate × 11.5) / 100

⇒ Rate = 100 / 11.5

⇒ Rate = 8.69%

**The annual rate of interest is 8.69%.**
